source_caption:
To preserve the absolute shock of John Doe’s sudden, blood-soaked introduction in the second half of the film, Kevin Spacey made an incredibly rare demand of the studio: he insisted on having his name completely scrubbed from the opening credits and all marketing materials. Since Spacey was a highly recognizable star at the time, he knew that if audiences saw his name billed alongside Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman, they would immediately deduce he was the mysterious serial killer. The studio ultimately agreed to the blackout, compensating Spacey by giving him top billing in the film’s closing credits instead. By intentionally stripping away his own star power and refusing to do any press, Spacey engineered one of the most terrifying, genuinely unpredictable cinematic entrances of the decade.
⠀
Seven (1995), directed by David Fincher, starring Brad Pitt, Morgan Freeman, Kevin Spacey. Two homicide detectives, a deeply cynical veteran on the verge of retirement and his fiercely arrogant new partner, are pushed to their absolute psychological limits while tracking a brilliant, impossibly cruel serial killer who is modeling his grisly murders on the seven deadly sins.

source_details.synopsis: Seven (often stylized as Se7en) is a 1995 American crime thriller film directed by David Fincher and written by Andrew Kevin Walker. It stars Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman, with Gwyneth Paltrow and John C. McGinley in supporting roles. Set in an unnamed, crime-ridden city, the narrative follows disenchanted, nearly retired Detective Lieutenant William Somerset (Freeman) and his newly transferred partner David Mills (Pitt) as they try to stop a serial killer from committing a series of murders based on the seven deadly sins.
